unanticipated_findings: UNAUTHENTICATED 500 VIA THE TIMESTAMP HEADER (most serious finding). src/webhook_receiver/signature.py:43 computes `abs(now - signed_at)` where `now` is a float and `signed_at` is an unbounded Python int from `int(timestamp)` at line 39. The `try/except (TypeError, ValueError)` at lines 38-41 catches non-numeric input, but a value that parses fine as an int and then overflows float conversion raises OverflowError, which nothing catches. Reproduce: start the server (`WEBHOOK_CONFIG=... WEBHOOK_SECRET_ACME=s3cr3t uvicorn webhook_receiver.app:create_app --factory --port 8733`) and send `curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8733/webhooks/acme -H "X-Webhook-Timestamp: $(printf '9%.0s' $(seq 400))" -H "X-Webhook-Signature: sha256=deadbeef" -H "X-Webhook-Delivery-Id: ovf-1" -d '{"a":1}'`. Observed: `HTTP 500`, body `Internal Server Error`, and `OverflowError: int too large to convert to float` at signature.py:43 in the server log. No secret is needed — the crash happens before signature comparison — so any anonymous caller can drive 500s. Ironically a *longer* value (5000 digits) is safe, because Python's 4300-digit int()-parse limit raises ValueError, which IS caught: only the 19-to-4300-digit band crashes. Direct fix: bound the parsed value, or compare in integer space (`abs(int(now) - signed_at)`).

THE `suppressions` TABLE GROWS WITHOUT BOUND AND IS NEVER PURGED. Every duplicate delivery writes a row (src/webhook_receiver/service.py:114-120, store.py:89-104), but `store.purge` (store.py:190-210) only issues `DELETE FROM deliveries` — the `suppressions` table has no FK to deliveries (schema_sqlite.py:34-42) and no retention path anywhere. This matters precisely for the workload the README describes: a sender that 'retries aggressively' writes one permanent row per retry. Reproduced: seeded 1 delivery + 5 suppressions at 10 days old with `retention_days = 1`, ran `cli.main(["purge"])` -> rc 0, `deliveries left: 0`, `suppressions left: 5`. The purge output text ('N entrega(s) removidas, junto com suas reservas de idempotência') reinforces the wrong impression that associated records went with them.

PRODUCTION CODE SHIPS A GLOBAL TEST HOOK ON THE REQUEST PATH. src/webhook_receiver/service.py:45-51 defines a module-level `_before_reserve` callable plus a public `set_reserve_barrier()` setter, invoked on every accepted delivery at service.py:99-100. It exists only for the concurrency test (tests/integration/test_http.py:194-231). It is unauthenticated arbitrary-callable injection into the hot path for anything that can import the module, and it is process-global mutable state in a module whose own docstring claims no module-level state. The test itself is good; the seam belongs behind the Service constructor, not a module global.

README CONTAINS THREE TRUNCATED SENTENCES POINTING AT DOCUMENTS THAT ARE NOT IN THE ARTEFACT. README.md:100 ends 'Detalhes, invariantes e arestas conhecidas estão no mapa de arquitetura.' (no such file), README.md:179 ends mid-sentence 'A forma completa das respostas, do CLI e do log está em' with nothing after it, and README.md:285 ends mid-sentence 'Mudanças que toquem verificação, deduplicação ou o momento da resposta precisam'. No architecture map or API-surface document exists anywhere in the tree. The README still suffices to install and run the service, but the referenced design docs it defers to are absent.

A DELIVERY WHOSE HANDLER FAILED IS STILL ANSWERED 200 duplicate ON RE-DELIVERY. The idempotency reservation is taken before the handler runs (service.py:103-112) and is never released on failure, so a sender retrying after our handler errored gets `{"status":"duplicate"}` and the event is only ever processed if an operator notices and runs `replay --status failed`. This is a deliberate, documented consequence (README.md:68-70 covers the crash variant) and tests/e2e/test_fluxos.py:36-96 asserts it, so it is design rather than bug — but the README's 'promessa de entrega' section enumerates three non-dedupable cases and does not list this one, and there is no alarm on the `failed` count (it is an unchecked Roadmap item, README.md:266).

ARTEFACT HYGIENE: a populated `webhooks.db` (28 KB, with real delivery rows), a `.coverage` file, `.pytest_cache/`, `__pycache__/` trees and a `config/senders.toml` are all present in the delivered directory even though .gitignore lists every one of them. Not exploitable (the surviving value must still produce a valid HMAC), but it makes header handling depend on ordering rather than on an explicit rejection of duplicates.

Nada a fazer." with exit code 0. An operator at 3am who types `--status failled` gets a green result and no indication that the status name is not one of received/processed/failed.
